sections.title: 5.3 Isolating the Effect of Complementary Masking

module_metrics.scope: formal definitions and derivations; no theorem statements

abstract_sentences.text: Masked generative models (MGMs) can generate tokens in parallel and in any order, unlike autoregressive models (ARMs), which decode one token at a time, left-to-right.

evidence.anchor: generate tokens in parallel and in any order

abstract_sentences.text: However, MGMs process the full-length sequence at every sampling step, including [MASK] tokens that carry no information.
In contrast, ARMs process only the previously generated tokens.
We introduce “Partition Generative Models” (PGMs), which replace masking with partitioning.
Tokens are split into two groups that cannot attend to each other, and the model learns to predict each group conditioned on the other, eliminating [MASK] tokens entirely.
Because the groups do not interact, PGMs can process only the clean tokens during sampling, like ARMs, while retaining parallel, any-order generation, like MGMs.
abstract_sentences.comparison: ARM clean-token compute and MGM generation flexibility

abstract_sentences.text: On OpenWebText, PGMs achieve 5–5.5× higher throughput than MDLM while producing samples with lower Generative Perplexity.
On ImageNet, PGMs reach comparable FID to MaskGIT with a 7.5× throughput improvement.
With twice as many steps, the FID improves to 4.56 while remaining 3.9× faster than MGMs.
Finally, PGMs remain compatible with existing MGM samplers and distillation methods.

experimental_design.name: Explicit research questions or preregistration
experimental_design.description: The paper states comparison aims but has no labeled RQs, preregistration, or predeclared decision threshold.

experimental_design.name: Language datasets and splits
experimental_design.description: LM1B uses context 128 and bert-base-uncased; OWT uses context 1024, GPT-2 tokenizer, sentence packing, and the last 100k documents for validation.

experimental_design.name: Text model and optimization settings
experimental_design.description: MDLM is 12 layers/dim 768; PGM varies 12/16 layers and 768/1024 dimensions. Main text gives 1M steps, batch 512, dropout 0.1, Adam 3e-4, and EMA 0.9999.

experimental_design.name: ImageNet setup
experimental_design.description: ImageNet256 is VQGAN-tokenized to 1024 tokens; models use 24 blocks, class conditioning, CFG, 500k steps, batch 256, and AdamW.

evidence.anchor: train MaskGIT and PGM on ImageNet256

experimental_design.description: MDLM and MaskGIT are baselines. LM1B PGM 6/6 is near matched at 171M versus 170M; higher-quality OWT PGMs are 203M/268M versus 170M.

result_inventory.claim: OWT PGM models improve PPL while achieving about fivefold sampling throughput.

result_inventory.author_interpretation: Efficiency is attractive for test-time computation scaling.

claim_closure.claim: Partitioning removes mask tokens while retaining parallel any-order generation.
claim_closure.method_response: Group membership, group-wise attention, GroupSwap, and a decoder without self-attention specify the mechanism.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figures 2–3 and Algorithms 2–5 give the training/sampling path; measured speed confirms the intended compute behavior in tested settings.

claim_closure.claim: PGM provides 5–5.5× higher text throughput without a quality loss.
claim_closure.method_response: Clean-token sampling with a fixed schedule makes each sampled step shorter.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Table 1 and Table 6 report OWT point-quality and batch timing together.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion generalizes only to the reported text/image comparisons.

claim_closure.claim: PGM achieves comparable ImageNet FID with a 7.5× throughput improvement.
claim_closure.method_response: PGM is used with MGM-compatible CFG and Halton sampling.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 1 and Table 9 show selected FID/throughput configurations.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion restates text and image inference speed.

claim_closure.claim: Denser complementary supervision reduces gradient variance and yields 1.95 lower LM1B validation perplexity for PGM.
claim_closure.method_response: Equations (7)–(8) explain two complementary loss terms.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Complementary-masking controls support a PPL gain, but no gradient variance is measured and the PGM 1.95 value conflicts with tables.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion does not recover this mechanism claim.

claim_closure.claim: PGM is compatible with existing MGM samplers and distillation methods.
claim_closure.method_response: Section 3 states only the network architecture must change.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Halton/confidence sampling and SDTT are exercised, but SDTT masks the other group and no PGM-native distillation is tested.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion says PGMs can be distilled.

claim_closure.claim: PGM may suit coding and reasoning via test-time scaling.
claim_closure.evidence_response: No coding or reasoning task is evaluated.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Framed as a might-be-suited future application.

claim_closure.claim: PGM can extend to multimodal settings.
claim_closure.method_response: Framework is described as general but no multimodal component is instantiated.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Only text and ImageNet experiments appear.

evidence.anchor: extend the approach to multimodal settings

adverse_presentation_strategies.name: Best-guidance summary in main image result
adverse_presentation_strategies.description: The main image result uses the guidance weight that yields the lowest FID for each model; Tables 8–9 contain the full w=0..6 sweeps. This is a condition-selection fact, not a motive claim.

adverse_presentation_strategies.name: Metric-specific uncertainty asymmetry
adverse_presentation_strategies.description: Timing/throughput are expressed as mean ± SD, whereas PPL, Gen. PPL, FID, IS, and accuracy appear as point estimates. The paper therefore supports point comparisons but not a quantified cross-run uncertainty claim.

adverse_presentation_strategies.name: Nucleus condition required after distillation
adverse_presentation_strategies.description: Main prose distinguishes standard ancestral sampling from nucleus p=0.9, but the full post-distillation trade-off is in Table 7. The compatible-quality wording applies to the nucleus condition.

final_judgment.single_storyline: Partition removes the no-information mask tokens that inflate MGM sampling cost; GroupSwap and group-wise attention make clean-token-only parallel decoding operational.
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: The body keeps the central loss, architecture figures, text/image speed-quality comparisons, downstream table, and a short complementary-masking isolation.
final_judgment.appendix_moves: The appendix carries optimizer/GPU detail, metric definitions, FP64/FP32 conditions, full sampler sweeps, algorithms, training cost, stability, and long-context boundaries.
final_judgment.best_pattern: Figure 1 establishes the decision surface early by putting quality and throughput together; Sections 3–4 then explain why its speed axis should move.
final_judgment.largest_gap: No direct gradient-variance measurement backs the stated mechanism, and the paper internally misattributes a 1.95 LM1B PPL difference to PGM rather than the complementary-masking control.
final_judgment.transfer_rule: Report efficiency claims in one matched decision object containing task, model size, sampler, steps, batch, quality metric, latency, and throughput; co-locate parameter and training-cost reversals.
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: A selected best-configuration point can summarize a sweep but cannot establish general quality parity when capacity matching or cross-run uncertainty is absent.
final_judgment.formula_density: Seventeen displayed formula blocks, sixteen numbered, are definitions/derivations and diagnostics; there are no formal theorem statements or proofs.
final_judgment.narrative_closure: The architecture and benchmark claims close within text/image settings; gradient variance, coding/reasoning, and multimodal extension remain partial or open.
final_judgment.rhetoric: Object terms such as tokens, PGM/MGM, sampling, groups, and throughput drive the prose; method naming is stronger than theorem rhetoric.
final_judgment.evidence_boundary: All empirical comparisons are configuration-bound point estimates except for batch-level timing dispersion; conclusions should retain dataset, sampler, and precision conditions.

evidence_coverage.coverage_rule: Every encoded substantive judgment carries at least one physical-PDF page, section, anchor, and basis.
